notes: The hardest case by design — real commitments buried in hedging and small talk. Tests: no invented due dates, correct handling of a genuinely unassigned/ambiguous owner, and NOT extracting hearsay/scheduling as if they were real tasks.

expectedItems.note: 'I'll try to circle back to it when I get a chance' has no real deadline — must not hallucinate one.
'Legal's been sitting on it forever' / 'pinged again, no response' is blocker language, even without an explicit 'we are blocked' statement.

optionalItems.note: 'Might be worth someone poking at it' names no one. Acceptable to extract as unassigned, or to skip entirely — NOT acceptable to confidently assign it to a specific named person, since no one volunteered.

forbiddenItems.reason: Secondhand hearsay about a vague 'vibe' from someone in design — not a real decision or commitment made in this meeting.
Pure meeting-scheduling logistics, not a task.
